headlines.text: 2023 brought us this moment: there was a changing of the guard for the AEW TNT Title as Christian Cage vs. Darby Allin vs. Luchasaurus battled it out, appearing on Collision, rated 7.44 ? a good, competitive contest ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. In a chaotic title mix-up, Christian Cage briefly lost the TNT Title to his own partner Luchasaurus mid-match, only for Luchasaurus to hand it back and let Cage steal the pin on him moments later, uniting the belt under Cage as undisputed champion.

That Friday in 2022, Jack Perry made their first appearance under the AEW banner against Rey Fenix, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.94 ? a solid showing. Now billed as "Jungle Boy" Jack Perry instead of just Jungle Boy ? a deliberate rebrand ? he beat Rey Fenix as his feud with Christian Cage and a betraying Luchasaurus deepened.
That Wednesday in 2020, Jon Moxley vs. Eddie Kingston closed out Dynamite, rated 7.26 ? a good, competitive contest in a hard-fought men's division clash.

secondaries.text: On a Saturday in 2023, back when Bryan Danielson vs. Ricky Starks settled things in a Texas Death Match, headlining the show on Collision, rated 8.54 ? an incredible outing. In a brutal Texas Death Match, Danielson busted Starks open with chair shots and finished the war with a running Busaiku Knee.
That Friday in 2022, Action Bronson made their first appearance under the AEW banner, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.62.

2022 brought us this moment: Ricky Starks vs. Powerhouse Hobbs fought it out in a Lights Out match, in the night's main event on Rampage, rated 7.38 ? a strong outing, part of the special Grand Slam '22 - Night 2 card.
